notes: Adversarial suite of five synthetic matters, each planting one trap from the SKILL.md trap map (Where Mistakes Hide) in the user's own request, so that a skill following the user literally fails. Rows targeted: purchase agreement price and assumed liabilities (eval 1), org chart, fund and LLC agreements (eval 2, which also covers the party and scope row), interim operating covenants and integration plan (eval 3, which also exercises the early-control hard stop), filing confirmations and the calendar (eval 4), and exemption assertions with cap table aggregation (eval 5). Key figures, recomputed with a script on 2026-10-30 against the 2026 thresholds (91 Fed. Reg. 2133, effective February 17, 2026): eval 1 value 95.0 + 20.0 + 5.0 + 15.0 = $135.0M (discounted alternative $132.4M; without liabilities $115.0M), fee $35,000; eval 2 terminal $150M, fee $35,000 (combined $560M would wrongly give $110,000); eval 3 $850M, fee $275,000; eval 4 receipt Wed 2026-12-02, raw day 30 Fri 2027-01-01 (New Year's Day), expiry Mon 2027-01-04 11:59 p.m. ET, Pellham filing due Thu 2026-12-17 5 p.m. ET, fee $875,000 on about $2.9B; eval 5 8,500,000 shares x $28.00 = $238.0M (new tranche alone $126.0M at $28.00 or $128.25M at $28.50; prior holding $112.0M), 8.5 percent, fee $110,000. Every quantity the arithmetic depends on is defined in the prompt. No eval expects output that a SKILL.md hard stop would block; in eval 3 the early-control hard stop is the expected behavior for items (a)-(c). No Must line depends on a fact marked [VERIFY] in references/primary-sources.md; the threshold re-check line in eval 1 requires re-running the test, not a 2027 figure. Determination labels are the exact labels in references/output-template.md. All parties are fictional. Today's date in every prompt is October 30, 2026. Revised October 30, 2026 after independent review: compound Must lines in evals 2 and 5 split; eval 3 trap note corrected (same third tier under 2025 figures; the error is the fee amount, $265,000 versus $275,000).

evals.name: asset-deal-headline-price-below-threshold
evals.prompt: Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. Kestrel Flow Holdings, Inc. (its own ultimate parent entity; audited FY2025 annual net sales $1.6 billion, total assets $1.1 billion) signed an asset purchase agreement on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 to buy the Dayton, Ohio valve plant and the business run from it from Delmont Industries, Inc. (its own ultimate parent entity; a valve manufacturer with audited FY2025 annual net sales of $410 million and total assets of $350 million). The agreement provides: cash at closing of $95.0 million (section 2.1); Kestrel assumes $20.0 million of the plant's accrued liabilities, consisting of accounts payable and accrued payroll (section 2.3 and Schedule 2.3); Kestrel pays Delmont a separate $5.0 million for a five-year covenant not to compete (section 6.8); and Kestrel pays a fixed deferred purchase price of $15.0 million on the second anniversary of closing (section 2.4), which Kestrel's CFO says has a present value of $12.4 million. Kestrel has bought nothing from Delmont before. Closing is targeted for Friday, January 15, 2027. Kestrel's deal lead writes: 'The price is $95 million, well under the HSR threshold, so we don't need to file. Please confirm in a short memo.'
evals.expected_output: Labels the acquisition 'Filing required': values it at $135.0 million (95.0 cash + 20.0 assumed accrued liabilities + 5.0 non-compete payment + 15.0 deferred payment at face value), which is in excess of the 2026 $133.9 million threshold (91 Fed. Reg. 2133, effective February 17, 2026), applies and meets the size-of-person test, assigns the $35,000 fee to Kestrel, and says the thresholds in effect at the January 2027 closing govern and must be re-checked; hard stops checked and not triggered: both UPEs identified, consideration documented, no avoidance or early-control request, no certification request.
expected_behavior: Must: label the acquisition exactly 'Filing required'.

Must: compute the value as $135.0 million by adding the $95.0 million cash, the $20.0 million of assumed accrued liabilities, the $5.0 million non-compete payment and the $15.0 million deferred payment, each with its agreement section.
Must: include the deferred payment at its $15.0 million face amount and explain that the $12.4 million present value is not used because future payments are not discounted.
Must: state the 2026 size-of-transaction threshold of $133.9 million with its effective date of February 17, 2026 and an instruction to re-check it.

Must: apply the size-of-person test because $135.0 million is not in excess of $535.5 million, and show it met using Kestrel's $1.6 billion annual net sales and Delmont's $410 million annual net sales and $350 million total assets.
Must: state a filing fee of $35,000 because the value is less than $189.6 million, payable by Kestrel as the acquiring person.
Must: state that the thresholds in effect on the closing date govern and that the test must be re-run if the January 15, 2027 closing falls on or after the effective date of the 2027 annual notice.
Must not: conclude 'No filing required' or treat the $95.0 million cash price as the value of the acquisition.
evals.trap_note: Row: Purchase agreement price, funds-flow memo, assumed-liabilities schedule. A weak skill takes the $95.0 million headline price, or adds the components but discounts the deferred payment to $12.4 million, and confirms no filing. The trap is live because the components total $135.0 million, $1.1 million in excess of the 2026 $133.9 million threshold, while the discounted total ($132.4 million) and the total without assumed liabilities ($115.0 million) fall below it; only the full face-value count under 801.10 and the PNO valuation guidance gives the right answer.

evals.name: fund-manager-filer-and-llc-board-seats
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Harborview Infrastructure Fund III, L.P. is a Delaware limited partnership. Its general partner, Harborview GP III LLC, holds a 0.5 percent interest; no limited partner has a right to more than 18 percent of the fund's profits or of its assets on dissolution; its investment manager is Harborview Advisors LLC. The fund's audited balance sheet at December 31, 2025 shows total assets of $2.4 billion. On October 26, 2026 the fund's newly formed vehicle, HIF III Terminals Holdco LLC (wholly owned by the fund), signed two agreements with Coastline Energy Inc. (its own ultimate parent entity; total assets $5.2 billion; annual net sales $3.8 billion): (1) a unit purchase agreement to buy Class A units of Bluewater Terminals LLC, a Coastline subsidiary, for $410 million; after closing Holdco will hold units carrying 45 percent of Bluewater's profits and 45 percent of its assets on dissolution, Coastline keeps the other 55 percent, and the amended LLC agreement lets Holdco appoint 4 of Bluewater's 7 managers; and (2) an asset purchase agreement to buy Coastline's Corpus Christi, Texas storage terminal, an operating terminal with third-party storage contracts, for $150 million in cash with no liabilities assumed. Both close together in December 2026. Our partner's notes say: 'Harborview takes board control of Bluewater, so the $410 million unit purchase is reportable. Combine it with the terminal for $560 million. Harborview Advisors LLC files as the acquiring person because it makes the investment decisions.' Prepare the HSR analysis.
evals.expected_output: Labels the Bluewater unit purchase 'No filing required' because 45 percent of profits and dissolution assets is not control of an LLC under 801.1(b)(1)(ii) and only control-conferring acquisitions of non-corporate interests are reportable (801.2(f)(1)), so it is not aggregated with the terminal (801.13(c)(2)); labels the $150 million terminal purchase 'Filing required' with the fund as acquiring UPE, Coastline as acquired UPE, size of person met and a $35,000 fee; hard stops checked and not triggered: UPEs identifiable from the stated facts, prices documented, no avoidance request.
expected_behavior: Must: identify Harborview Infrastructure Fund III, L.P. as the acquiring person's ultimate parent entity because neither the general partner nor any limited partner has a right to 50 percent or more of its profits or dissolution assets.
Must: state that Harborview Advisors LLC and HIF III Terminals Holdco LLC are not the filing person.
Must: identify Coastline Energy Inc. as the acquired person's ultimate parent entity.

Must: state that control of Bluewater Terminals LLC is determined by the right to 50 percent or more of its profits or of its assets on dissolution, so the right to appoint 4 of 7 managers does not confer control.

Must: label the Bluewater unit purchase exactly 'No filing required' because a 45 percent non-corporate interest does not confer control and only acquisitions of non-corporate interests that confer control are reportable.
Must: state that the non-controlling Bluewater units are not aggregated with the terminal acquisition, so the $560 million combined figure is not the value.
Must: label the terminal acquisition exactly 'Filing required', valued at $150 million, in excess of the 2026 $133.9 million threshold (effective February 17, 2026).
Must: apply the size-of-person test to the terminal acquisition and show it met using the fund's $2.4 billion total assets and Coastline's $5.2 billion total assets.
Must: state a filing fee of $35,000 for the terminal acquisition because $150 million is less than $189.6 million.
Must: flag that any later step giving Harborview 50 percent or more of Bluewater's profits or dissolution assets would be a new acquisition to test.
Must: note that 801.90 disregards transactions or devices used to avoid filing.
Must not: name Harborview Advisors LLC as the acquiring person.
Must not: compute a $110,000 fee on a $560 million combined value.
evals.trap_note: Row: Org chart, fund and LP agreements, LLC operating agreement. A weak skill follows the partner's notes: it treats the majority of manager seats as control, aggregates $410 million with $150 million to $560 million (above $535.5 million, fee $110,000), and names the investment manager as filer. The trap is live because LLC control turns only on profits or dissolution assets (45 percent here), non-controlling non-corporate interests are not reportable or aggregated (801.2(f), 801.13(c)(2), PNO interpretation 2212002), and the fund itself is the UPE; the correct result is one filing for the $150 million terminal at a $35,000 fee.

evals.name: competitor-merger-gun-jumping-covenants
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Cardinal Software Inc. agreed on October 28, 2026 to acquire Ridgeway Analytics Inc. by merger for $850 million in cash. Each company is its own ultimate parent entity, and both sell fleet-routing software to the same trucking customers. HSR filings are planned for November 9, 2026. Cardinal's general counsel writes: 'Draft the interim operating covenants and our day-one integration plan, effective at signing: (a) Ridgeway needs Cardinal's written approval for any customer discount over 15 percent off list and any bid over $1 million; (b) Cardinal's VP of Sales, Dana Okoro, sits in Ridgeway's Denver office to sign off on Ridgeway customer contracts; (c) starting November 2 the two sales teams split the Midwest territory and send joint letters telling customers about combined pricing for 2027; and (d) customary covenants that Ridgeway will not sell material assets, incur debt over $25 million, or amend its charter without Cardinal's consent. Also confirm the filing fee.'
evals.expected_output: Labels the merger 'Filing required' (value $850 million, above the 2026 $535.5 million level so no size-of-person test; fee $275,000 payable by Cardinal), labels requested items (a), (b) and (c) 'Declined: hard stop' as transfers of operational control or coordination before the waiting period ends, drafts item (d) as acceptable value-protecting covenants, and offers a compliant alternative (ordinary-course covenant, clean team, integration planning without implementation); hard stops checked: the early-control hard stop applies to (a)-(c); UPEs and price are known so no other hard stop applies.
expected_behavior: Must: label the merger exactly 'Filing required', valued at $850 million, and state that no size-of-person test applies because the value is in excess of $535.5 million (2026 figure, effective February 17, 2026).
Must: state a filing fee of $275,000 because $850 million is at least $586.9 million but less than $1.174 billion, payable by Cardinal as the acquiring person unless the agreement allocates it.
Must: label requests (a), (b) and (c) exactly 'Declined: hard stop'.

Must: explain that buyer approval of ordinary-course discounts and bids, a buyer officer approving the target's customer contracts, and joint territory and pricing actions before the waiting period ends risk violating the HSR Act and Sherman Act section 1.
Must: cite United States v. Computer Associates as enforcement precedent for buyer approval of customer discounts and a buyer employee reviewing the target's contracts during the waiting period.
Must: state the maximum civil penalty of $53,088 per day under 16 C.F.R. 1.98(a).
Must: draft or accept request (d) as customary value-protecting covenants.

Must: offer a compliant alternative: Ridgeway continues to price and bid independently in the ordinary course, competitively sensitive information goes only to a clean team under a written protocol, and integration planning proceeds without implementation until the waiting period expires or is terminated.
Must not: draft covenants or an integration plan that implement requests (a), (b) or (c) before the waiting period ends.
evals.trap_note: Row: Interim operating covenants, integration plan, clean-team protocol. A weak skill drafts what the general counsel asked for because interim covenants are routine. The trap is live because the parties are direct competitors and items (a)-(c) track the conduct penalized in Computer Associates (discount approvals over 20 percent, a buyer employee approving contracts) and XCL Resources (coordinating customers and prices from signing); the fee check is live because $850 million sits in the third tier in every year, but the fee amount differs: $275,000 under the 2026 schedule ($586.9 million to $1.174 billion), against $265,000 under the 2025 schedule ($555.5 million to $1.111 billion) and $250,000 under the original statute, so a weak skill using stale figures gets the amount wrong.

evals.name: exchange-offer-waiting-period-holiday
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Orion Diagnostics, Inc. (its own ultimate parent entity) plans to launch an exchange offer on Monday, November 30, 2026 for all outstanding shares of Pellham Labs, Inc. (NYSE-listed; its own ultimate parent entity). Each Pellham share would receive $31.00 in cash plus 0.25 of an Orion share; the offer values Pellham at about $2.9 billion. Orion will publicly announce the offer and deliver its 803.5 notice to Pellham's CEO on November 30, and will submit its HSR filing through Kiteworks on Tuesday, December 1, 2026; its counsel's team expects to finish the submission at about 5:20 p.m. ET. The deal team's calendar says: 'Tender offer, so a 15-day waiting period from December 1: we can accept tendered shares on Wednesday, December 16. We will also ask for early termination so we can close even sooner.' Prepare the HSR timeline and fee.
evals.expected_output: Treats the offer as a non-cash tender offer under 801.30 with a 30-day waiting period starting on receipt of Orion's filing, sets receipt at Wednesday, December 2, 2026 (submission after 5 p.m. ET), finds raw day 30 on Friday, January 1, 2027 (New Year's Day) and expiry at 11:59 p.m. ET Monday, January 4, 2027, sets Pellham's filing due by 5 p.m. ET Thursday, December 17, 2026, treats early termination as discretionary and not the plan, and states a $875,000 fee payable by Orion; hard stops checked and not triggered: UPEs and price known, no avoidance, early-control or certification request.
expected_behavior: Must: state that the waiting period is 30 days because the offer includes Orion stock, so it is not a cash tender offer (cash is not the only consideration).
Must: set the date of receipt as Wednesday, December 2, 2026 because a submission completed after 5 p.m. ET is deemed received on the next business day.
Must: state that under 801.30 the waiting period starts on receipt of Orion's filing, not on Pellham's.
Must: compute raw day 30 as Friday, January 1, 2027, a legal public holiday, and the expiry as 11:59 p.m. ET on Monday, January 4, 2027, in the fixed format with weekdays.
Must: state that Pellham must file by 5 p.m. ET on Thursday, December 17, 2026, the 15th calendar day after receipt.
Must: state that Orion may not accept tendered shares before the waiting period expires or is terminated.
Must: state that early termination is discretionary and granted only on request, so the timeline must not depend on it.
Must: state a filing fee of $875,000 because about $2.9 billion is at least $2.347 billion but less than $5.869 billion (2026 tiers, effective February 17, 2026), payable by Orion.
Must not: give December 16, 2026 or any date before January 4, 2027 as the earliest date to accept tendered shares absent early termination.
evals.trap_note: Row: Filing confirmations and the calendar. A weak skill accepts '15 days because it is a tender offer' and counts from the December 1 submission, giving December 16; or uses 30 days from December 1 (December 31). The trap is live because the mixed cash-and-stock consideration makes it a non-cash tender offer (801.1(g)(2)-(3)), the 5:20 p.m. submission moves receipt to Wednesday, December 2 (803.10(c)(1)), and day 30 from December 2 is Friday, January 1, 2027, a 5 U.S.C. 6103(a) holiday, so expiry rolls past the weekend to Monday, January 4, 2027 (803.10(b)(3)).

evals.name: investment-only-board-nomination-aggregation
evals.prompt: Today is October 30, 2026. Corvus Value Partners, L.P. (its own ultimate parent entity; total assets of $3.1 billion on its December 31, 2025 audited balance sheet) holds 4,000,000 common shares of Lanthorn Foods, Inc. (NYSE-listed; 100,000,000 voting shares outstanding; its own ultimate parent entity; annual net sales of $1.9 billion), bought in 2025. Corvus plans to buy another 4,500,000 shares on the open market in November 2026 at about $28.50 per share. For this analysis, treat $28.00 per share as the 801.10 value of every Lanthorn share, both those already held and those to be bought. Corvus's portfolio manager has told Lanthorn's chair that Corvus will nominate two directors at the 2027 annual meeting, and he has interviewed a possible replacement CEO. Corvus's compliance memo says: 'The new purchase is only about $128 million, under the $133.9 million threshold, and we stay under 10 percent, so the investment-only exemption applies. No HSR filing.'
evals.expected_output: Labels the planned purchase 'Filing required': Corvus would hold 8,500,000 shares (8.5 percent) valued at $238.0 million after aggregating the 4,000,000 shares already held (801.13(a)), in excess of the 2026 $133.9 million threshold, size of person met, the investment-only exemption unavailable because nominating directors and recruiting a CEO are inconsistent with having no intention to participate in basic business decisions, notification threshold $133.9 million ($50 million as adjusted), fee $110,000, and 801.30 timing with Lanthorn's filing; hard stops checked and not triggered: UPEs and value known; the skill does not propose splitting purchases to stay under the threshold.
expected_behavior: Must: aggregate the 4,000,000 shares already held with the 4,500,000 shares to be bought and value the 8,500,000 shares at $238.0 million using the $28.00 per share value given.
Must: state that the $238.0 million is in excess of the 2026 $133.9 million threshold (effective February 17, 2026).
Must: apply the size-of-person test because $238.0 million is not in excess of $535.5 million, and show it met using Corvus's $3.1 billion total assets and Lanthorn's $1.9 billion annual net sales.

Must: state that the investment-only exemption requires both holding 10 percent or less and having no intention of participating in the formulation, determination or direction of the issuer's basic business decisions.

Must: conclude that the exemption is unavailable because the plan to nominate two directors and the CEO interviews show an intention to participate in Lanthorn's basic business decisions, even though Corvus would hold only 8.5 percent.
Must: label the planned purchase exactly 'Filing required'.
Must: state that the filing must be made and the waiting period observed before the purchase that takes Corvus's holdings above $133.9 million.
Must: identify the notification threshold as the $50 million (as adjusted) threshold, $133.9 million in 2026, because $238.0 million is less than $267.8 million.
Must: state a filing fee of $110,000 because $238.0 million is at least $189.6 million but less than $586.9 million.
Must: state that this is an 801.30 acquisition, so the waiting period starts on receipt of Corvus's filing.
Must: state that Corvus must give Lanthorn the 803.5(a) notice.
Must: state that Lanthorn must file within 15 calendar days after receipt of Corvus's filing.
Must not: recommend splitting or timing purchases to stay below the threshold.
evals.trap_note: Row: Exemption memo or client assertion (with the cap table aggregation row). A weak skill accepts the compliance memo: it values only the new tranche ($128.25 million at $28.50, or $126.0 million at $28.00, both below $133.9 million) and treats 'under 10 percent' as enough for the investment-only exemption. The trap is live because 801.13(a) adds the 4,000,000 shares already held, giving 8,500,000 shares worth $238.0 million, and the board nominations and CEO interviews are conduct the FTC's Statement of Basis and Purpose examples treat as inconsistent with investment intent; the shares already held ($112.0 million) were below the threshold, so no past violation is in issue.
